target_customer: Designers, artists and teams who create 3D content and want real time multiplayer collaboration
problem: 3D design tools were single user desktop apps, making collaboration slow.

founders.name: Phillippe Siclait
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; has made 3D games since middle school.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time multiplayer 3D editing in the browser needs WebGL, sync and conflict handling, hard for a five person team.

defensibility.rationale: Collaboration alone was copyable by Figma and 3D tool vendors; no data or network effects were visible.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent action found; the company is listed Inactive.

market_need_then: Figma showed demand for multiplayer design tools and 3D content was growing for web, games and e-commerce, but no demand evidence specific to Clay was found.

branding.domain_note: Used clay3d.io rather than clay.com; no purchase history found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Pitched as Figma for 3D, collaborating in 3D should feel magical

brand_strength.rationale: Search found no press or community about this Clay; results were dominated by unrelated Clay products.

outcome_analysis: Clay aimed to be Figma for 3D and is marked Inactive by YC. No shutdown notice, post-mortem or funding news was found in searches, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty. The generic name made the company hard to find in search.
notes: Website clay3d.io did not resolve in this session (treated as unreachable or dead). Competitor search found only undated pages (Spline, Vectary, Womp); none dated near the batch, so the list is empty. Seedtable lists a Clay entry whose funding was paywalled; unverified.
